summary: ZFS root snapshot rollback left /etc/grub.d immutable and prevented boot after depot reimage
description: Issue summary: Several laptops failed to boot after depot reimage. Impact: Devices land in grub rescue due to missing grub.cfg apply; recovery attempts show /etc/grub.d/ files with immutable attribute set (i). Environment: corporate depot reimage pipeline, Ubuntu 22.04-based gold image with ZFS root snapshot workflow. Steps to reproduce and logs below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start with device on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with ZFS root and active snapshot set by imaging-runbook
2) In depot, run imaging pipeline that restores zpool from snapshot and runs chroot to regenerate initramfs and update-grub
3) Observe pipeline succeeds but device reboots to grub rescue with 'unknown filesystem' or 'file not found'
4) Mount root on rescue media and inspect /etc/grub.d — files show immutable attribute (lsattr shows 'i') preventing update-grub writeouts
5) Attempting to remove immutable bit (chattr -i) fails when executed in chroot during pipeline because of snapshot mounts being read-only overlayed by ZFS snapshot restore step
logs: imaging-runner.log: 2026-03-09T02:12:34Z INFO restored zpool 'rwdpool' from snapshot 'gold-2026-03-08'
imaging-runner.log: 2026-03-09T02:13:10Z ERROR chroot: failed to write /etc/grub.d/40_custom: Operation not permitted
dmesg snippet: [    6.123456] ZFS: mounted rwdpool/ROOT@gold-2026-03-08 read-only
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: snapshot restore left certain datasets mounted read-only or with properties that propagate immutable flag to file attributes.

Confirmed: imaging pipeline uses zfs receive to restore snapshot and then mounts datasets; a legacy step from older runbook sets zfs property 'readonly=on' briefly for validation and forgets to unset on specific dataset 'rwdpool/ROOT'.

Observed the immutable attribute appears to have been applied earlier by preflight hardening script (pre-imaging-lockdown.sh) which marks some config files immutable during snapshot creation. Those attributes persisted in snapshot and were not cleared during restore.

Reproduction on spare lab device: restored snapshot, then within rescue chroot unable to write to /etc/grub.d until chattr -i executed on host (not chroot). When chattr -i executed in host context the files became writable and update-grub regenerated grub.cfg successfully.

Risk: Any automated pipeline that runs update-grub inside chroot will silently fail and leave device unbootable if immutable bits are present. Affects all images created with the legacy lockdown script and ZFS snapshot workflow.
temporary_workaround: Manual recovery: boot rescue USB, mount ZFS root, run chattr -i on files under /etc/grub.d from host context (not chroot), chroot and run update-initramfs -u and update-grub, then reboot.

For bulk recoveries at depot: run a pre-exit hook on imaging host that runs 'zfs mount -o remount,rw <dataset>' and then 'xargs -0 chattr -i <list-of-config-files>' on the restored dataset before chroot step.
resolution: Short-term fix applied 2026-03-11: imaging-runbook updated to include post-receive cleanup step that clears immutable attributes for known config paths and ensures zfs property readonly is unset on ROOT dataset before chroot.

Automation change committed: https://github.com/redwood-infra/imaging-scripts/pull/422 merges cleanup hook and a verification step that attempts to write a temp file in /etc/grub.d to validate writability.
Follow-up: schedule run to reimage affected devices in depot; flagged ~24 devices from repair queue that used the gold snapshot created between 2026-02-20 and 2026-03-08.
Long-term: retire pre-imaging-lockdown.sh pattern that sets immutable bits and adopt content-versioning via config-management agent so snapshots do not rely on file attributes for security hardening.
next_steps: 1) Ops to run remediation script on 24 affected depot devices by 2026-03-15
2) Imaging team to include unit test in CI that verifies grub regeneration after restore
3) Security and Image teams to agree alternative hardening approach by 2026-03-25
4) Postmortem document to be created and linked to this ticket after full sweep
5) Notify Helpdesk to escalate any incoming 'grub rescue' returns from depot as high priority and reference this ticket
